edition.alertText: Houthi drone strikes Saudi Jazan oil refinery — kills Nepali maintenance worker, first fatality at a Saudi refinery since war began; Iranian drone kills 2 Italian Rheinmetall defence technicians at Kuwaiti military facility — first Western European military casualties of war; Italy summons Iranian ambassador, PM Meloni calls deaths 'act of aggression against an Allied nation'; NATO SecGen Rutte expresses 'grave concern'; IRGC claims 2 tankers hit mines near Khasab — engine-room fires, crews evacuating; ADNOC confirms crew member death from Nov 18 Hormuz transit attack — total maritime casualties reach 56; Saudi coalition intercepts fresh wave of missiles and drones at Riyadh and Eastern Province; coalition sustains Yemen air campaign — fresh strikes on Dhamar, Taiz targets; oil rallies sharply — Brent ~$95.58 (+2.71%), WTI ~$84.70 (+1.26%) as Jazan and mine attacks stoke supply fears; gold steady ~$3,579; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 — 2 days away; IEA surplus and 1.7M b/d glut make output expansion fraught; fertilizer through Hormuz zero for ninth month; QatarEnergy LNG force majeure through December; EU gas storage 74.33% — lowest in decade entering winter

situation: Oil rallied sharply on Thursday as escalating attacks across the Gulf stoked fresh supply fears, with Brent settling near $95.58/bbl (+2.71%) and WTI at approximately $84.70/bbl (+1.26%) — both recovering from Wednesday's modest rebound and extending the bounce from Monday's three-month lows near $88 Brent. The rally was fueled by a Houthi drone attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil refinery that killed a Nepali maintenance worker — the first fatality at a Saudi refinery since the war began in February — and IRGC claims that two tankers struck mines near Khasab, Oman, with engine-room fires reported on both vessels. The mine campaign continued to broaden: having targeted crude tankers, container ships, and LNG carriers in rapid succession over the past week, Iran's naval forces now appear willing to strike any vessel category in or near the strait. Hormuz oil flows remained depressed at approximately 9.5–10 million barrels per day, down from the 17.15M b/d pre-war baseline, with the Hormuz Strait Monitor noting only 2 vessels transited in a 24-hour period on November 24 versus a pre-war average of approximately 60 — traffic at roughly 3% of normal. The contango in Brent futures eased slightly as the Thursday rally narrowed the spread, though the market structure remains bearish compared to October's backwardation. Gold edged up to approximately $3,579/oz (+0.62%), stabilizing after weeks of decline from the wartime peak of $5,608. The OPEC+ meeting scheduled for November 29 — now two days away — remains the key near-term catalyst, with the IEA's declaration of the first supply surplus since the war and Deutsche Bank's estimate of a 1.7M b/d glut in October making any output expansion discussion deeply fraught. Aramco's December Arab Light OSP cut of $2 to -$6.50 to Oman-Dubai — the steepest discount since May 2020 — signals that the buyer's market is firmly entrenched despite continued physical disruption.

The conflict's geographic and political scope expanded sharply as an Iranian drone killed two Italian Rheinmetall defense technicians at a Kuwaiti military facility — the first Western European military casualties of the nine-month war and a stark escalation of Iran's willingness to target NATO-allied personnel in Gulf states. Italy summoned Iran's ambassador and Prime Minister Meloni called the deaths 'an act of aggression against an Allied nation,' while NATO Secretary General Rutte expressed 'grave concern' — language interpreted as a step toward potential Article 5 consultations if attacks on allied personnel continue. Kuwait, which has already suffered IRGC drone attacks on Ali Al-Salem Air Base and Patriot air defense systems since mid-November, condemned the strike. The Italian deaths compound a pattern of expanding Iranian targeting: Bahrain's Sitra oil facility struck November 21, Kuwaiti bases hit November 18, and now Western military advisors killed on allied soil. Meanwhile, ADNOC confirmed the death of a crew member from the November 18 attack on one of its logistics vessels transiting the Strait, bringing the total maritime conflict death toll to at least 56 with approximately 120 injured across 307 total attacks since February. Diplomacy remained frozen: Iran continues to insist on all seven preconditions before engaging in talks, with the senate's failure to pass a binding war powers resolution leaving the Trump administration with unchecked authority to continue operations. Trump's comment that the war is 'funded through January' was widely interpreted as signaling at least two more months of military operations absent a breakthrough, while Iran's Navy reiterated that the Strait 'will never be reopened' until all demands are met. The OPEC+ meeting on Saturday looms as a pressure test: with IEA confirming the first supply surplus since the war began and Saudi production running at 8.3M b/d (HSBC Q4 forecast) versus the 6.3M originally projected, the cartel faces a stark choice between defending price or defending market share.

The Yemen front remained a theater of intense combat as the Saudi-led coalition sustained its air campaign following the previous day's 654-strike barrage, with fresh raids targeting Houthi missile storage facilities in Dhamar and launch sites in Taiz governorate. The Houthis continued to threaten Saudi infrastructure, with a fresh wave of drones and ballistic missiles intercepted over Riyadh and the Eastern Province — though the coalition's Iron Dome-augmented defenses have held. The dual-chokepoint risk persists: Houthis have consolidated their control of fortified positions near Bab al-Mandeb and advanced within 60–70 kilometers of Aden, raising the specter of simultaneous disruption at both the Strait of Hormuz and the southern Red Sea passage. On the supply chain front, fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain at zero for the ninth consecutive month, with the UN warning that 45 million people face severe food insecurity and the FAO Food Price Index at 136, its highest since November 2022. QatarEnergy's LNG force majeure extends through December — the eighth consecutive extension since April — while EU gas storage sits at 74.33%, the lowest in over a decade entering winter. The convergence of an OPEC+ meeting in two days, the first Western European military fatalities, an expanding Iranian mine and missile campaign targeting all vessel categories, the first Saudi refinery death, and deepening winter energy stress across Europe and Iran itself points to continued high volatility through the week. The post-Thanksgiving danger window identified by analysts remains open as US markets close early on Friday and return in full force Monday.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for ninth consecutive month — March through late November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warned 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urged US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260, with 10,519 wounded; more than 1,600 dead and 300,000+ displaced since July (UN); UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children. Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr, oil-linked, through 2034) citing ongoing force majeure (S&P Global Platts, Nov 11). DES NW Europe LNG benchmark at $27.59/MMBtu on Nov 11, up 175% YoY. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). 31 laden LNG tankers exited Hormuz in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~EUR89.59/MWh (~$100.85); EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). Natural gas futures fell 8.2% to $3.13/MMBtu (Nov 23). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). IRGC claims LNG tanker hit mine in eastern Hormuz — first LNG carrier explicitly targeted, AIS off at time of strike (Nov 25); escalation to LNG vessels raises winter supply concerns for Europe and Asia. IRGC mine campaign now hitting crude tankers, container ships, and LNG carriers — no vessel type safe. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs EUR2B higher amid Iran war. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels. Iran braces for winter natural gas shortages — imposes power cuts as energy crisis deepens (Nov 23).

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030. Arabian Gulf crude shipments fell 27.6% YoY to 531.3M tonnes in Jan-Oct 2026 — Gulf share of global seaborne crude fell from 39.8% to 30.6% (Banchero Costa/LSEG).
